repository.name: kopitiam-pos
repository.description: Nanyang Kopi & Toast - Self-Order Kiosk, Kitchen Docket Printer & Payment POS

issues.title: Kiosk Step 2 'Kopi O Kosong' freeze & POS kitchen docket label coupling
issues.body:
In yesterday's Raffles Place kiosk trial, 19 of 28 first-time users (68%) froze for over 2 minutes on Step 2 ('Kopi O Kosong', 'Kopi C Siew Dai', 'Teh Halia'), and 72% missed the small top-right language toggle.

Why renaming the buttons to 'Black Coffee No Sugar' failed at Tampines:
- In POS v2.4, button `display_name` prints straight onto the kitchen thermal docket (`ticket_label`). When English names printed on kitchen dockets at Tampines, our 65-year-old kopi uncles slowed down by 15 seconds per cup.
- The 15-inch screen only fits 12 buttons per page (max 18 chars). Adding two-line subtitles pushes half the drinks onto Page 2.

POS v2.4 technical specification: `kitchen_print_name` is a separate config field from `display_name` (1 hr setup), and the 2-step Milk & Sugar pop-up modal module takes 1.5 hrs to configure.

issues.title: 28-seat morning crunch: tissue-packet chope-ing & laptop wall-socket campers
issues.body:
Our Raffles Place shop has only 28 seats. Between 8:00am and 10:00am, office workers leave tissue packets on empty tables before joining the 15-minute queue, while freelancers buy one $2.20 Kopi O and camp at our four 4-seater booths (16 seats) for 2 hours using the 12 wall power sockets and free Wi-Fi. That costs us about $420 every morning in lost breakfast turnover.

Floor notes from Wei Ling & Mei:
- Auntie Mary (62) got yelled at by a customer in a suit when she moved his tissue packet last week, and she will not play seat police or touch customer belongings.
- 60% of our morning customers dine solo and cannot carry a hot tray of runny soft-boiled eggs without a table.
- Store electrical spec: the 12 booth wall sockets and guest Wi-Fi router run on a programmable smart relay breaker in the back room.

issues.title: Cashless-only kiosks turning away elderly regulars with $2 notes
issues.body:
Our Raffles Place kiosks only take PayNow QR and cards. Yesterday 14 retired morning regulars walked out angry when told we don't take $2 notes, and a TikTok clip of a 74-year-old uncle looking lost at our 'NO CASH' sign hit 40,000 views.

Counter and floor constraints:
- Our internal counter hygiene SOP keeps money handling separate from ready-to-eat food: any staff member who handles coins or notes must remove gloves and wash hands before slicing kaya toast or cracking soft-boiled eggs (+40s per order), and counting the cash float at night costs $380/month in overtime.
- The toast counter runs on two staff at the 8am rush, so there is no spare pair of hands to take cash and make change without slowing orders.
- 94% of retired morning regulars carry only $2 or $10 notes, so a $2.20 Kopi always needs change; they refused a $20 minimum stored-value card yesterday.
- Auntie Mary (62) is the only floor staff who seats solo diners with hot trays and clears tables, so she cannot be pulled off the floor to run a cash point.
- Physical cash bill-acceptors for the kiosks cost $1,400 and take 3 weeks to arrive, and there is no spare till or cashier terminal at the front.

issues.title: @MakanWithZack viral 'shrinking butter slice' video & takeaway melt root cause
issues.body:
Food TikToker @MakanWithZack (85k followers) posted a reel (90,000 views) claiming our Kaya Butter Toast has half as much cold butter as Ya Kun. He offered to film a live re-taste tomorrow at 8:30am for $600 cash, or $450 + 20 Kaya Toast plushie keychains (we have $750 left in our launch budget), provided every regular customer gets the exact same standard.

Kitchen & margin notes:
- Wholesale Anchor Golden Salted Butter went up 35% last month. Doubling the butter slab from 12g to 20g across all sets wipes out $0.42 per set ($1,100/month in margin).
- Our 12g cold butter slab did not shrink: it stays thick on dine-in open plates, but melts flat when sealed inside a closed takeaway box with hot toast unless packed in a separate chilled cup on the side ($0.05/box) or in a vented box.
